newsitem.title: FRANCE: Chirac says "cohabitation" should run full course.
newsitem.headline: Chirac says "cohabitation" should run full course.

text.p: French President Jacques Chirac said on Monday he thought his "cohabitation" power-sharing with Socialist Prime Minister Lionel Jospin would run its full course until 2002 provided the government did not cause a crisis.

"The parliamentary majority has been elected for five years. It is up to the government to act in such a way that no crisis occurs which could call that contract into question," Chirac said in his first television interview since the combined left defeated his centre-right coalition in a June 1 election.

Asked whether he expected such a crisis, he said: "I do not wish that." Asked whether he expected the legislature would run its full term, the president, who has the right to dissolve parliament after it has sat for one year, said: "I think so."
Chirac said he wanted a "constructive cohabitation" with Jospin and declined to criticise the red-pink-green coalition government, saying he would wait to see what intiatives it took.

He sought to mark out a broad role for himself, going beyond the traditional presidential domains of defence and foreign affairs into maintaining social cohesion and upholding France's high-technology industries and scientific research.

Recalling his presidential aims of modernising France, upholding its place in the world and maintaining the balance of its institutions, he said: "If these are also the government's aims, there will be no problem...That would be constructive cohabitation."
